CheckTitle: Ensure IAM policies do not allow privilege escalation actions
Description: IAM customer-managed and AWS managed policies attached to principals must not contain permissions enabling documented IAM privilege escalation paths. Escalation-capable actions include iam:CreatePolicyVersion, iam:AttachRolePolicy, iam:CreateLoginProfile, iam:UpdateLoginProfile, iam:SetDefaultPolicyVersion, and iam:UpdateAssumeRolePolicy.
Risk: Principals with privilege escalation capabilities can modify IAM policies, attach admin policies to themselves, or create new admin credentials. This allows an attacker who compromises any escalation-capable account to achieve full account control.
Remediation: Review all attached policies for escalation-capable actions. Restrict iam:* actions to only those strictly required. Apply resource-level restrictions where possible. Use IAM Access Analyzer to identify over-permissive policies.
SeverityBasis: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 AC-6 (Least Privilege), CM-5 (Access Restrictions for Change). The specific action set is author-selected based on IAM permission evaluation semantics documented in AWS IAM documentation. High severity reflects that these actions directly enable full account control. Severity is assigned by the framework's three-tier classification model defined in docs/severity_classification_model.md; no primary source publishes a severity scale for this specific action-set pattern.
AuthoritativeSource: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5; AWS IAM documentation — Security best practices in IAM
CISControl: N/A — privilege escalation action-set detection is not a numbered control in CIS AWS 3.0.0; grounded in NIST AC-6
ThreatReference: IAM privilege escalation via permission modification actions is widely documented in AWS cloud security research literature
